- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.16) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid underreaction.  
- Model often overreacts to recent price highs; apply mean reversion: if forecast > 20% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 10–15% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.23, -0.16, +0.23), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
